title: Migration Amendment (Streamlining Visa Processing) Bill 2019
portfolio: Immigration, Citizenship, Migrant Services and Multicultural Affairs

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would let the minister decide which visa applicant groups must submit biometric data for their application to be accepted.
An application would be invalid if a required person does not supply a facial image, fingerprints or another personal identifier, and the minister could also allow other ways to provide them.
The government says the change is needed because checks of biometrics against law enforcement and partner-country databases have found hidden criminal histories and identity discrepancies.
changes: Give the minister power to specify groups of visa applicants who must provide one or more personal identifiers for a valid application.
Make a visa application invalid if the applicant does not supply the required personal identifiers.
Allow personal identifiers to be given through an identification test or another method the minister sets.
summary.affected: Visa applicants in groups specified by the minister.

divisions.question: Migration Amendment (Streamlining Visa Processing) Bill 2019 - Second Reading - Stop privatisation

speeches.speaker: Michelle Landry
speeches.brief: The Migration Amendment (Streamlining Visa Processing) Bill 2019 makes the collection of personal identifiers a prerequisite for a valid visa application, supports electronic lodgement and efficient processing, and aims to enhance visa program integrity and protect Australians from criminal and national security threats.
